hero.subtitle: We stand on the sandbars of Qigu, using British L1A1 rifles to guard our borders. For we know, even as the sea winds howl, our rifles have sand cuts.

articles.title: Insisting on the L1A1: The Soul in the Sea Wind and Sand Dust
articles.excerpt: The Central Military Commission announces that the Tai-Kang Forces will not follow the SA80 trend...
articles.content: The Central Military Commission announces that the Tai-Kang Forces will not follow the SA80 trend. Our rifles must be British inch-pattern, and must have "sand cuts" to survive on the sandbar. This is not just a matter of armaments, but our insistence on our origins. The L1A1 is not just a rifle; it is the symbol of our Tai-Kang spirit: simple, robust, and capable of surviving in the harshest environments. All members of the Kiaⁿ-soàⁿ Infantry must be familiar with every part of this rifle.

articles.title: How to "mock" an undemocratic main island?
articles.excerpt: The writers of the plains write: "The people on the main island are living in fear of the white terror..."
articles.content: The writers of the plains write: "The people on the main island are living in fear of the white terror, yet they cannot see the tranquility of our sandbar." Using 19th-century art to explain the sorrow of the 20th century. In the Tai-Kang Federal Republic, we do not need to fear the government, because we are the government. We build our dreams on the sandbars; though the sea wind is strong and sand blows into our eyes, our hearts are free. The people on the main island pursue money; we pursue the sovereignty to speak out loud.

articles.title: Inner Sea Trade Agreement Signed
articles.excerpt: Today, the Tai-Kang Federal Republic and neighboring sandbar tribes reached a trade consensus...
articles.content: Today, the Tai-Kang Federal Republic and neighboring sandbar tribes reached a trade consensus. This agreement will ensure the free flow of salt, dried fish, and imported materials within the Inner Sea region. This is a major step forward in our country's diplomatic history. Although our country is still in exile, our economic autonomy cannot be ignored. The trade representative noted that future focus will be on building better supply lines to support the frontline Kiaⁿ-soàⁿ Infantry.

articles.title: A Look Back at the 1860 Inner Sea Treaty
articles.excerpt: Historians have reinterpreted the 1860 Inner Sea Treaty, the cornerstone of our nation...
articles.content: Historians have reinterpreted the 1860 Inner Sea Treaty, the cornerstone of our nation. Back then, witnessed by the British and local forces, the status of these neutral sandbars was established. The treaty explicitly stated that no external power shall interfere with the internal affairs of the Inner Sea. This ancient document remains our most powerful legal basis against external regimes. Research indicates that the parties involved fully considered the unique geography of the sandbars, which explains why we have maintained our independence for so long.
